title: Study Shows Vaccines Cause Autism

claims.text: Vaccines contain harmful toxins that cause autism in children.
claims.explanation: No credible study has ever shown a link between vaccines and autism. The original study was retracted and debunked.

claims.text: Thimerosal, a preservative in vaccines, is the cause of rising autism rates.
claims.explanation: Thimerosal was removed from childhood vaccines in 2001, yet autism rates continued to rise - disproving the link.

claims.text: A 1998 study by Dr. Andrew Wakefield confirmed the vaccine-autism link.
claims.explanation: Wakefield's study was retracted by The Lancet in 2010. He lost his medical license for falsifying data.

claims.text: The CDC conducted a study on 95,000 children and found no link between vaccines and autism.
claims.explanation: This is accurate - the CDC published a large-scale study in 2013 confirming no link.

claims.text: Parents are reporting that their children developed autism symptoms immediately after vaccination.
claims.explanation: Anecdotal reports exist but are not scientific evidence. These are coincidental timing events, not causal.

trust_score_description: Very Low - Only 1 out of 5 claims has credible sources
